notes:
**A site whose pages are all JavaScript shells is described as one.**

Docket refuses to conclude that something is missing site-wide when every page
it read was an empty shell — it saw the shell, not the content, and cannot say
what is or is not in there. That refusal was right and the explanation attached
to it was written for a different problem. On a site where all 221 pages are
shells and none were missed, the report said "found at least 0 more it did not
reach — about 100% of the site … because most of it was never seen", under the
heading "Only part of the site was crawled", and advised re-running with a
higher page limit.

Nothing was missed and a bigger page limit changes nothing. That case now says
what actually happened, and points at the remedy that would change the answer.

**`docket serve --host` explains what it costs.**

The local API has no authentication because it is only meant to be reachable
from your own machine, and the default binds to loopback. The flag that changes
that had no help text at all. It now says what binding elsewhere exposes.
